overview.problemStatement: Operators need a restricted back office to manage users, events, registrations, and admin access, and to attribute every administrative change.
overview.proposedSolution: A role-gated /admin area with Clerk sign-in, invite-only signup, a client guard plus server requireAdmin, platform totals, user/event/registration management, a rate-limited invitation lifecycle with Resend email and daily expiry, an append-only audit log, analytics queries, and admin email preferences.
overview.targetAudience: Ivent staff holding the admin or super_admin role.
assumptions: retroactive: true - documented from the existing implementation during brownfield onboarding; it is not a forward-looking product decision.
super_admin is the only role that may change roles and manage invites; admin can view and moderate non-admin users.
Invite emails are sent by the client after the invite record is generated.
Analytics are computed on read over full collections; no warehouse exists.
outOfScope: Editing an event from the admin console.
Granular per-permission roles beyond user, admin, and super_admin.

userStories.title: Restrict the back office to administrators
userStories.benefit: ordinary users cannot read or change platform data

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a signed-out visitor or a user, /admin/* redirects to /admin and the guard renders no protected content; given admin or super_admin the console renders; every admin Convex function also calls requireAdmin.

userStories.title: See platform totals
userStories.benefit: I can see the size of the platform at a glance

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given I open /admin/dashboard, I see total users, total events, total registrations, and upcoming event counts, with a loading state and an access-denied state on error.

userStories.title: Moderate users
userStories.want: to search users and control bans and roles
userStories.benefit: abusive accounts and staffing changes are handled

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the users page, I can search by name or email and see role and ban state; I can ban or unban a non-admin, banning another admin is rejected, and only a super_admin can change a role.

userStories.title: Oversee events
userStories.want: to inspect and delete any event

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the events page, events are listed and searchable by title; deleting one requires confirmation, removes its registrations, and writes an event.deleted audit entry.

userStories.title: Oversee registrations
userStories.want: to review registrations and cancel a ticket

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the registrations page, rows show attendee, event, and status, and a confirmed row offers a cancel action with confirmation.
Given a super admin submits an email, a pending invite with a seven-day expiry is created or refreshed, generation is limited to ten per minute, and the invites page can send the code through Resend.

userStories.title: Accept an invite
userStories.want: to sign up with my code

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a signed-in user submits an email and matching pending, unexpired code, the invite becomes accepted and the user role becomes admin; missing, accepted, revoked, expired, or mismatched codes are rejected.

userStories.title: Manage the invite lifecycle
userStories.want: to revoke, delete, resend, and expire invites

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a pending or expired invite, a super admin can revoke, delete, or resend a new code and expiry; accepted invites cannot be revoked, deleted, or resent; the daily cron marks pending invites past expiry as expired.

Given an administrative mutation, an auditLogs entry records actor, action, target, label, optional metadata, and time; the audit page supports text search and action filtering and shows total, 24-hour, and 7-day counts.
Given the analytics page, user growth, event growth, registration trend, events by category, top events, events by city, and summary metrics are available for the selected window.

userStories.title: Control admin email preferences
userStories.want: to choose which notification emails I receive

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the settings page, I can view and update emailOnNewEvent, emailOnNewRegistration, emailOnNewAdminInvite, and emailOnNewUser, and they persist on my user record.

functionalRequirements.text: The admin area MUST be restricted to admin and super_admin on both the client and the Convex server.
The dashboard MUST report total users, events, registrations, and upcoming events.
User management MUST support search, ban and unban, and role change with the documented role rules.
Event management MUST support listing, search, cascading delete, and audit logging.
Registration management MUST list registrations and expose a confirmed-row cancel action.
Invite generation MUST be super-admin-only, rate-limited, seven-day expiring, and emailable.
Invite acceptance MUST validate status, expiry, and code before promoting the user to admin.
Invite lifecycle MUST support revoke, delete, resend, and daily expiry.
Administrative mutations MUST write audit entries, and the audit page MUST support search, filter, and summary counts.
Analytics MUST expose growth, trend, category, top-event, city, and summary queries.
Admin settings MUST persist the four email preferences.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Every admin Convex function MUST call requireAdmin; the client guard is defense in depth only.
Invite generation MUST be rate-limited and invites MUST expire after seven days.
Administrative mutations that change users, events, invites, or registrations MUST create an audit entry.
Admin screens MUST remain usable at a 360px viewport with loading and empty states.
The feature MUST pass ESLint, TypeScript checking, and SpecDrive governance validation.

edgeCases.description: A non-admin calls an admin function.
An admin tries to ban another admin.
A non-super-admin tries to change a role or manage invites.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The action is rejected with a super-admin-only error.

edgeCases.description: An invite is accepted, revoked, or expired.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The conflicting action is rejected with the specific reason.

edgeCases.description: The invite email fails to send.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The invite record remains and the error is surfaced to the caller.

edgeCases.description: There are no users, events, registrations, or audit entries.
An admin cancels another user's registration.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The attendee ownership check currently rejects it; see RISK-001.

risks.description: The admin registrations page calls the attendee cancelRegistration mutation, which enforces registration.userId === ctx.user._id, so an admin cannot cancel another user's ticket and no registration.cancelled audit entry is written.
risks.mitigation: Add an admin-authorized cancellation mutation that logs registration.cancelled, and route the admin UI through it.

risks.description: getAllUsers searches only the first 100 users returned, so search can miss accounts as the user base grows.
risks.mitigation: Add a bounded indexed search or server-side pagination.

risks.description: requireAdmin re-queries the user on every admin call.
risks.mitigation: Acceptable at current scale; revisit if admin traffic grows.

risks.description: Analytics reads whole collections per query.
risks.mitigation: Introduce precomputed aggregates if collections grow large.
